recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中大量紅血球表面有數目不一、長短不齊、分布不規則的尖刺突起，且多數細胞緻密、缺乏中央淡染區，這就是棘狀紅血球（acanthocyte, spur cell），配合肝硬化病史即為 spur cell anemia。
features: Numerous acanthocytes: dense red cells with few irregularly spaced spicules of varying length
Admixed crenated cells with more regular short projections (echinocyte-like forms)
Many acanthocytes are small and lack central pallor
Occasional elliptocytes/ovalocytes and target-like cells in the background
Neutrophils and a monocyte show unremarkable morphology; platelets present
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked poikilocytosis dominated by acanthocytes, which are dense, spheroidal red cells bearing a small number of irregularly spaced, unequal spicules. Crenated cells with more regular projections are admixed, along with occasional ovalocytes and target-like forms. Leukocytes and platelets are morphologically unremarkable, and no schistocytes or red cell agglutination are evident. Findings are consistent with acanthocytosis (spur cell anemia) in the setting of advanced liver disease.

ddx.vs: Echinocytes have 10-30 short, evenly spaced, uniform projections around the whole circumference and often retain central pallor, whereas acanthocytes have fewer irregular spicules of unequal length.
Morphology of the acanthocytes is identical, so distinction relies on the clinical context (neurologic disease, fat malabsorption, low apolipoprotein B) rather than liver disease.
Spherocytes are dense and lack central pallor but have smooth round contours without spicules.
Fragmented cells show one or two horn-like projections with sharp straight edges from mechanical damage rather than multiple irregular spicules on a spheroidal cell.
